posts.author: gstv87
posts.body:
there's two ways to go at it:
way 1: the "jump" method.
-cut the sprite's head in a graphic program and save both halves as character sprites (they don't need animation, you can set the container event to 'direction fix')
-put the sprites on individual events out of reach, on standby.
-on cue, teleport the events on top of one another (the transparency of the image should sell the effect, so keep both halves at their relative position in the sprite sheet) and force the head event to move-route jump away from the body.
way 2: the "composite" method.
-make the animation in one sprite sheet, as big as it needs to be.
-add a note tag to the event in question, to grab it from the code.
-add a code snippet to the loading of that event's sprite, to align it to the grid (it will try to appear centered to the sprite cell, not the feet of the character, so offset it to place)
one method requires two events, the other one event and a bit of coding.
either way, you can still use one single sprite sheet: one with static images, the other with the full animation complete with blood and effects.

You're talking about a few different things at the same time.
An Animation is not a Character. Their spritesheets are formatted entirely differently, and $ and ! have nothing to do with animations.
For that matter, $ and ! don't just arbitrarily fix things
The formats for both characters and animations are in MV's instructions, if you click Help -> Contents -> Documentation -> Asset Standards, you can find and read the standards for both file types there.
It doesn't sound to me like just getting an animation and playing it on the target is going to look exactly like what you want, I would draw it into the spritesheet and use move routes to turn the character to different frames to show the blood moving (just like the Quick Event Creation does for doors and chests).

Make two pages for the NPC sprite. First page is normal sprite. Second page is without head. Then make a red color edit of the rtp fountain water sprite. Also make a picture of the cut head you edited in gimp.
When the head slice happens turn a switch to the second page of the sprite. Turn a blank event above to the red fountain water sprite and put stepping on and make it play a gush sound effect. Show the picture of the head, put rotate picture on and use move picture x 2 to make the head fly up and down in a parabola. And also put the jump1 sound effect when the head flies.

I am not sure if GIMP should be your first choice in that case. But since you already started out on it, you might as well continue. So for the aforementioned tile set, you would want to set the grid in GIMP to 48 by 48. This is to ensure that you don't cut out too much or too little. If you set "snap to grid" to ON, your mouse will be guided by a magical nudge now and then to keep you from straying from the grid. Cut out the graphics that you want, and paste them in a 3x4 grid, like you see with other PNGs in img/characters.
